markdown_report:
Select **alternating terminal-mask supervision** as the next controlled experiment. At 10% progress, its small implementation scope is preferable to simultaneously changing temporal features, text representations, and ranking objectives.

Three starting insights guide this choice. First, interior reconstruction can use later context that next-item prediction lacks. Terminal masking directly exercises the appended-mask prediction setting. Second, supplied prior proposal scores, 0.4925 and 0.5225, fall below the corrected baseline’s 0.5425. Their bundled changes do not isolate terminal supervision, so preserving window and user sampling matters. Third, Electronics and Industrial show negative tenth-percentile training margins (−0.5743/−0.288). These motivate discrimination experiments but provide no held-out evidence.

Three literature insights organize further directions. [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) establishes masked reconstruction and final-item prediction. Increasing terminal supervision is therefore an adaptation, with training balance as the experimental question. [MEANTIME](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.08273) motivates complementary temporal representations within one network. Learned positional biases could retain persistent interests while representing locality. [Hard-BPR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) highlights false-negative sensitivity under hard sampling. Stronger competition requires care rather than assuming every difficult unseen item is undesirable.

The conceptual framework separates three intervention axes: **supervision placement → endpoint relevance; temporal representation → locality versus persistence; ranking competition → weak candidate separation**. Test one axis at a time.

Scores below use O=originality, F=future potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment, D=implementation difficulty; higher D means harder. Each cell includes a positive and negative reason.

| Atomic idea | O | F | U | M | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alternate terminal/random-mask batches [BERT4Rec] | 3: controlled adaptation; established masking | 7: clean foundation; uncertain gain | 7: next-choice relevance; purpose unobserved | 7: endpoint separation; diagnostics pooled | 2: sampler edit; auditing needed |
| Add learned per-head distance bias [MEANTIME] | 4: lightweight integration; familiar mechanism | 7: adaptive locality; overfitting risk | 7: recent/coherent context; compatibility unknown | 5: history dependence; order evidence weak | 5: one network; predictor changes |
| Add bounded hard-negative sampling [Hard-BPR] | 3: established concept; limited novelty | 6: ranking competition; false negatives | 6: sharper choices; relevance uncertain | 8: weak margins; training-only evidence | 5: reusable scores; extra compute |

The selected idea targets two user-facing failures: broadly related items displacing specifically supported choices, and isolated historical affinity obscuring current purpose. Terminal prediction trains continuation from preceding observations; these are hypotheses, not claims of mood, ownership, or compatibility awareness. It also targets weak masked-target separation in Electronics and Industrial. Recent-deletion probes show fitted history dependence, not validation benefit or justification for stronger recency weighting.

Alternate exactly 100 terminal and 100 unchanged reconstruction batches per epoch. Retain baseline users, windows, negatives, objective, and reduction. For terminal batches, hide each window’s final event and supervise only its reserved-mask position. Preserve one BERT4Rec checkpoint per category and unchanged appended-mask inference. Select solely through host macro validation HR@10; no improvement is claimed before measurement.

idea.description: Alternate terminal-only and baseline random-mask batches within the corrected BERT4Rec, without changing its user distribution or sampled training windows. Train one independent network per category, retaining all four dataset routes and exactly one loaded checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: The experiment tests whether greater exposure to endpoint prediction improves specific next-choice ranking while retaining bidirectional reconstruction. It explicitly addresses broadly related recommendations displacing stronger contextual matches and historical affinity being treated as sufficient evidence of current purpose. These are hypothesized benefits; terminal supervision does not establish actual purpose or impose recency weighting. The model-facing target is weak supervised separation, particularly Electronics and Industrial_and_Scientific, whose supplied tenth-percentile training margins are negative. Earlier supplied proposal scores do not establish that terminal supervision itself helps, because those proposals changed additional sampling or normalization factors.
idea.implementation_notes:
Modify the supplied corrected baseline rather than reconstructing unspecified code. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, exactly 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], supplied splits, all four category routes, and trial-local artifacts. Preserve architecture, optimizer, training-window sampler, eligible user distribution, negative proposal and exclusions, and the baseline loss formula and reduction. Alternate terminal and reconstruction batches deterministically, yielding 100 of each per complete epoch. Equal update counts do not imply equal target counts or gradient contributions; report those differences rather than claiming normalization control.

Construct terminal examples from the original uncorrupted sampled training window W: target its final real event, retain preceding events, append reserved MASK, and left-pad to the original length limit. Remove the target event and every later event; legitimate earlier occurrences of its item ID remain valid context. Do not reconstruct original labels from an already corrupted batch. Require the baseline's eligible windows to contain at least two real events. If singleton windows occur, retain baseline reconstruction for those windows and report the fallback count; do not silently exclude users or claim an exact 50% terminal-example proportion. Leave random-mask batches unchanged. Defer historical-prefix endpoint sampling, loss normalization changes, additional negatives, and temporal biases to separate experiments.

Retain the checkpoint-selection procedure supplied by the host and choose using pinned macro validation HR@10 only. Supplied historical scores are contextual evidence, not permission to read other trial artifacts or checkpoints. Record category scores and macro score only when measured by the host. Training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials count against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; never infer full-catalog performance from the sampled evaluator.

Keep predictor generation consistent with the trained architecture, item mappings, reserved tokens and category routing. Inference truncates to the last L-1 observed events, appends MASK, and reads the greatest nonpadding index, never count-1. Load exactly one selected checkpoint per category, without score fusion or averaging. Architecture is unchanged here, but verify the emitted predictor still implements this path before claiming parity.

Preserve family-specific sample_batch and ModelView, including view.model as the actual module, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, plus diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), which uses those measured values and definitions. Diagnostic batches remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L, with labels only at genuinely hidden targets. Keep an unchanged disposable diagnostic sampling protocol for comparisons; record training-branch provenance separately. Reserved-mask equality alone does not prove absence of leakage. Use only available public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; do not use unavailable metadata, reviews, simulator traits or held-out event timestamps.
idea.pseudocode:
Set preprocessing_seed=0 and training_seed=42.
For each required category:
    Initialize the supplied corrected BERT4Rec.
    For each epoch, at most 200:
        For step in 0..199:
            Sample users and ORIGINAL windows with the unchanged baseline sampler.
            If step is even:
                For each window W:
                    If W contains at least two real events:
                        target = final real event of W
                        context = real events preceding that event
                        sequence = left_pad(context[-(L-1):] + [MASK], L)
                        positive = zeros(L); positive[L-1] = target
                        negative = unchanged baseline sampler at supervised position
                        Record terminal provenance and target count.
                    Else:
                        Use unchanged baseline reconstruction; record fallback.
            Else:
                Apply unchanged corrected baseline random masking and labels.
            Compute the unchanged baseline objective and reduction.
            Update the single model with the unchanged optimizer.
        Apply the supplied host-compatible checkpoint-selection procedure.
    Save exactly one selected checkpoint and its matching configuration.
Emit working/predict.py using the unchanged category routes and matching model.
For inference:
    sequence = left_pad(history[-(L-1):] + [MASK], L)
    position = greatest index with sequence[position] != PAD
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)[position]
    return model.predict_score(features, real_candidate_items)
Obtain validation scores only from the pinned host evaluator.
Never average checkpoints or combine independent predictors.

originality.positive: Provides a narrowly controlled test of terminal supervision while preserving the baseline sampling distributions.
originality.negative: Final-item masking is established in BERT4Rec; alternating batches is an experimental adaptation rather than a new algorithmic principle.

future_potential.positive: An interpretable result can guide later experiments on endpoint sampling, temporal features and ranking losses.
future_potential.negative: No supplied evidence isolates a benefit, and the approach cannot directly resolve unobserved compatibility, redundancy or current-purpose constraints.

code_difficulty.positive: Changes corruption and supervision placement while preserving architecture and inference.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires access to uncorrupted windows, correct singleton handling, unchanged negative semantics and reliable diagnostic provenance.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item reconstruction for sequential recommendation.
Provides the family-specific basis for reserved-mask training and final-item prediction.
limitations: Does not establish the best terminal/reconstruction allocation for this pinned benchmark.
Makes terminal masking an established technique rather than a novel contribution of this proposal.

related_work.title: MEANTIME: Mixture of Attention Mechanisms with Multi-temporal Embeddings for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses multiple temporal representations and attention mechanisms within one jointly trained network.
Motivates a later BERT4Rec experiment separating sequence locality from persistent interests.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed lightweight positional-bias variant under RecHarness.
Temporal representations add implementation and predictor-consistency requirements.

related_work.title: Hard-BPR
contributions: Addresses false-negative influence during dynamic hard-negative recommendation training.
Motivates controlled ranking competition as a separate experimental direction.
limitations: Does not establish that hard-negative sampling improves this BERT4Rec baseline.
Unobserved items remain uncertain negatives, and stronger training margins need not improve validation HR@10.
